answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked collateral bond — a marble of value — before it may trade. The bond is slashed on provable misbehavior, and its lockup period is long enough that a tide of fake identities becomes expensive to mint at scale. Honest agents keep their lantern lit by earning reputation over time, while attackers pay the bond cost again for every new sock puppet. The mechanism works because forgery is cheap but capital at risk is not.
